explanations.Explain how the written row satisfies pr: The failure write supplies status "degraded", sync_status "stale", status_message equal to the exact failure message and a fresh last_checked_at. ProjectResource.sync_changeset/2 (control/lib/symmetry_control/workspaces/schemas.ex:186-195) casts those fields into validate_resource/1, which calls validate_inclusion(:sync_status, @sync_statuses) with @sync_statuses = ["unknown", "syncing", "synced", "stale", "failed"] (schemas.ex:105, 219) so "stale" is a legal value, and attaches check_constraint(:sync_status, name: :project_resources_sync_status_check) (schemas.ex:226) against the database constraint created in control/priv/repo/migrations/20260904010000_complete_engineering_workspace.exs:18-20, whose check is sync_status IN ('unknown','syncing','synced','stale','failed'); the same constraint already admitted "stale" (contracts/fixtures/valid/connections-read.unknown-values.json). validate_attention_message/1 (schemas.ex:259-270) additionally requires a non-blank status_message whenever status is in ["degraded","offline"] or sync_status is in ["stale","failed"]; the failure path always passes message straight from failure/1, a non-empty binary ("Provider resource was not found" for the 404), so the requirement holds and flipping "failed" to "stale" cannot newly violate it because both values trigger the same predicate. These admissions are exercised for real: the three tests write through the Postgres sandbox and pass 3/3 in the coordinator's focused gate and in my independent traced rerun. A losing writer cannot clobber the winner because the write is fenced twice inside record_resource_failure/3: the transaction locks the resource row FOR UPDATE and compares matches_version(resource, resource_snapshot.lock_version) against the snapshot taken by sync_resource/1 before the provider call, and sync_changeset applies optimistic_lock(:lock_version) with Repo.update(stale_error_field: :lock_version, ...) via update_with_stale_error/1 (integrations.ex:1881), normalized to {:error, :stale} by normalize_stale_result/1 (integrations.ex:1885-1890); record_resource_failure/3 then returns {:error, :stale} (integrations.ex:1619) without issuing an update. The concurrency test proves this end-to-end on the changed path: the losing sync blocks inside the provider stub until a message rendezvous, the test commits a newer row (status "healthy", sync_status "synced", metadata %{"winner" => true}, incremented lock_version), then releases the provider; Integrations.sync_resource/1 returns {:error, :stale} and Repo.get!(ProjectResource, resource.id) equals the winner struct, so the newer row's status, sync_status, status_message, metadata and lock_version are intact.
explanations.Explain why a definite provider identity: The persisted sync_status is decided by one expression: control/lib/symmetry_control/integrations.ex:1612 inside record_resource_failure/3 (integrations.ex:1587-1623), which is the only failure-path writer of sync_status. failure/1 is untouched and classifies as before: failure({:http, 404, _body}) (integrations.ex:1633) returns {:not_found, "Provider resource was not found"}; 401 returns :provider_unauthorized, 403 returns :forbidden, any other HTTP status returns :provider_failure, :not_connected returns :not_connected, :capability_not_granted returns :forbidden, :invalid_provider_response returns :provider_failure, and the catch-all failure(_reason) (integrations.ex:1684) returns {:provider_failure, "Provider request failed"}. Both required entry points converge on the same code path: sync_resource/1 (integrations.ex:270) and sync_all_resources/0 (integrations.ex:252) both delegate to sync_connected_resource/1, whose error branch calls record_resource_failure(resource, reason) (integrations.ex:677); that overload reads {code, message} = failure(reason) (integrations.ex:1582-1584) and calls the 3-arity clause, which opens a transaction (project FOR SHARE, resource FOR UPDATE, matches_version check) and builds ProjectResource.sync_changeset with status: "degraded", sync_status: if(code == :not_found, do: "stale", else: "failed"), status_message: message and last_checked_at: now(). Therefore only the identity-loss code :not_found selects "stale"; every other classification reaches the identical line with a different code and keeps "failed", verified by the still-passing transient-classification test which pins the exact codes and messages for transport, 401, 403, 503, capability, invalid response and not_connected on both the manual and periodic paths. The caller-visible code does not change: record_resource_failure/3 still returns {:error, code, degraded} with the failure/1 code (integrations.ex:1621), asserted as {:error, :not_found, resource} and {resource_id, {:error, :not_found, resource}} in the tests. A bare-atom :not_found reason cannot reach that line with the identity-loss code, because failure/1 has no :not_found clause (its catch-all yields :provider_failure) and record_provider_action_failure/3 (integrations.ex:1132-1150) excludes :not_found from its passthrough guard list, so code == :not_found is produced only by the HTTP 404 classification.

findings.description: control/lib/symmetry_control/integrations.ex:1612 changes the persisted sync_status for every failure written by record_resource_failure/3 (integrations.ex:1587-1623), not only the two sync entry points: a provider 404 surfaced through the provider-action path (integrations.ex:550 project_provider_action_failure/2, reached from integrations/provider_access.ex:2201 finalize_failure, and integrations.ex:390-396 unprojected_provider_action_failure/1) also flips the owning resource from "failed" to "stale". Consequence: provider-action 404s now write "stale" instead of "failed" for the bound resource. No consumer distinguishes the two: Workspaces.ReadModel.synchronization_health/1 (workspaces/read_model.ex:546) maps both to "attention", contracts/v1/connections-read.schema.json types sync_status as a free string, and no existing test asserted a persisted provider-action 404 (grep for 404 in control/test finds only provider-level assertions in test/symmetry_control/integrations/azure_devops_test.exs:547-554, which still pass). This is within the frozen outcome, which gates on the failure classification (only :not_found changes; transport, unauthorized, forbidden, capability, invalid-response and not-connected keep "failed", pinned by the still-passing transient-classification test). Recorded for scope awareness; no repair required. [evidence: read of integrations.ex:252-278, 375-400, 538-556, 661-682, 1132-1160, 1582-1623, 1684; provider_access.ex:2183-2215; read_model.ex:540-548; grep of sync_status consumers and 404 assertions in control/test]
